html:
The map's label for the Sinhalese states of Sri Lanka in 800, 1492 and 1500.

In 800 the island was still ruled from Anuradhapura, the old Buddhist capital of the Sinhala kings. The Cholas sacked it in the early 1000s. The capital moved to Polonnaruwa, and later shifted south and west as power drifted from the dry north.

By 1492 the island was divided. The Kingdom of Kotte, near modern Colombo, was the main Sinhalese power. Parakramabahu VI (1412 to 1467) had briefly united the whole island from there. The hill kingdom of Kandy was breaking away in the centre, and the Tamil Jaffna Kingdom held the north. In 1505 the Portuguese arrived, and over the next century they took the coasts, leaving Kandy as the last independent Sinhalese kingdom.
